results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Single Arm Rear Delt Row
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handle to about chest height. Stand facing the handle, holding one handle with an overhand grip (palm facing down), and lean back slightly with your arm extended and feet shoulder-width apart.
Engage your arm and pull your chest towards the handle by bending your elbow and driving it out to the side, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine.
Continue pulling until your upper arm is parallel to the floor and your elbow is bent at a 90-degree angle.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
tips: Focus on using your rear deltoid and upper back muscles to perform the row, avoiding excessive use of your arm.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull your chest towards the handle and inhale as you extend your arm back.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Single Arm Rear Delt Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Split Fly
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the handles with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand with an overhand grip (palm facing down) with the left hand and an underhand with the right (palm facing up).
Engage your core and lean back slightly with your arm extended, keeping your body straight from head to heels and your arms extended in front of you at shoulder height.
Spread your arms in front of you, bringing your left arm overhead and the right arm by your hip, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly bring your arms back together to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Start with a smaller range of motion and gradually increase as your strength and flexibility improve.
Ensure your wrists are straight and not bending during the movement.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you open your arms and inhale as you bring them back together.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Split Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Trap Bar Shrug
instructions: Stand in the center of a trap bar with your feet shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees and hips to lower your body, and grasp the handles of the trap bar with a neutral grip (palms facing in).
Stand up straight with the trap bar at arm's length by your sides, keeping your core engaged and back straight.
Lift your shoulders towards your ears, squeezing your traps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you shrug your shoulders and inhale as you lower them.
Keep your neck relaxed and avoid straining it during the movement.
Ensure your back remains straight and avoid leaning forward or backward.
results.description: Trap Bar Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a trap bar, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Upright Row (Front View)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Allow the barbell to rest against your thighs with your arms fully extended.
Pull the barbell upward along the front of your body by bending your elbows and lifting your upper arms.
Continue lifting the barbell until it reaches chest height, keeping your elbows higher than your wrists throughout the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Lead with your elbows to ensure proper muscle engagement and avoid wrist strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift the barbell and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the barbell.
results.description: Barbell Upright Row (Front View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

results.name: Upright Row Cable Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of a resistance band, holding a handle in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing back). Ensure the band is taut when your arms are extended downwards.
Lift the handles straight up towards your chin, leading with your elbows and keeping the band close to your body.
Raise the handles until your elbows are slightly higher than your shoulders and pointing to your sides.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you lift the handles and inhale as you lower them.
Use a resistance band that allows you to maintain control and proper form throughout the exercise.
Avoid lifting the handles too high, which can put unnecessary strain on your shoulder joints.
results.description: Upright Row Cable Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

results.name: Upright Row Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing your thighs). Let the dumbbells rest against your thighs.
Lift the dumbbells straight up towards your chin, leading with your elbows and keeping the weights close to your body.
Raise the dumbbells until your elbows are level with your shoulders, ensuring your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you lift the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
Focus on using your shoulders and upper back to lift the dumbbells, avoiding excessive use of your biceps.
Avoid lifting the dumbbells too high, which can put unnecessary strain on your shoulder joints.
results.description: Upright Row Dumbbell is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

results.name: Upright Row EZ Bar
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ Bar with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Allow the barbell to rest against your thighs with your arms fully extended.
Pull the EZ Bar upward along the front of your body by bending your elbows and lifting your upper arms.
Continue lifting the EZ Bar until it reaches chest height, keeping your elbows higher than your wrists throughout the movement.
Slowly lower the EZ Bar back to the starting position by extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Lead with your elbows to ensure proper muscle engagement and avoid wrist strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift the barbell and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the EZ Bar.
results.description: Upright Row EZ Bar is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with an ez barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

results.name: Upward Rotation Bent Arms
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent at 90 degrees with your upper arms parallel to the floor, and your forearms pointing down to the floor.
Rotate your forearms upwards until your fingers point towards the ceiling, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Slowly rotate them back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions
tips: Focus on using your shoulder muscles to rotate your arms, avoiding excessive use of your neck or back.
Keep your upper arms stationary throughout the movement to ensure proper form.
Lift your arms as high as comfortable, to avoid unnecessary strain on your shoulder joints.
results.description: Upward Rotation Bent Arms is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Rotator Cuff.

results.name: Weighted Standing Shoulder Press With Plate
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate with both hands at chest level, elbows bent and pointing down.
Press the plate upward by extending your arms fully above your head, keeping your core tight and your back straight.
Lower the plate back down to chest level in a controlled manner.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you press the plate up and inhale as you lower it down.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the press to keep tension on your shoulder muscles.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees for better balance and support.
results.description: Weighted Standing Shoulder Press With Plate is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Abdominal Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and drawn towards your chest.
Wrap your arms around your knees, hugging them tightly.
Hold the stretch in this position, allowing your back to round slightly and your head to relax forward.
After holding the stretch for the desired amount of time, release your arms and return to a neutral sitting position.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid hunching them up towards your ears.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
Perform the stretch slowly and avoid any sudden movements to prevent strain.
results.description: Abdominal Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Lower Back.
